First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{3}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{-2{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}}{6{x}^{3}-9} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{(\frac{-2{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{6{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}-\frac{9}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{(-2+\frac{1}{x})}{(6-\frac{9}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & =\frac{-2+0}{6-0} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
